previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, severe headache, and back pain following a lumbar puncture three weeks prior. Her symptoms were attributed to a gastroparesis flare and migraine exacerbation, possibly worsened by dehydration and muscle tension. She had leukocytosis on admission that resolved, and Group B Strep was found in urine without symptoms, deemed asymptomatic. Peritoneal fluid showed no signs of infection. She was treated with IV anti-nausea medication, erythromycin for gastroparesis, uptitrated topiramate for migraines, and short-term oxycodone for pain. Her oral intake improved, vital signs stabilized, and she was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up plans for pain management and integrative medicine.

was triggered by an LP. The LP was done in ___ and 
since that time, the headache has been severe and persistent. 
She describes the headache as ""every nerve ending in my body 
exploding."" She points to the back of her head and says that she 
feels like a ""rock hit me in the back of the head."" It is 
bilateral and wraps around to the front. The pain is throbbings, 
and constant. It has not gone away in three months. She feels 
that the triptans have helped somewhat but she never gets enough 
doses and had to pay out of pocket for some so she stopped 
taking them. This medication is really the only thing that's 
helped so far. She has tried Fioricet, oxycodone and others she 
can't remember in the past without any effect. There is no 
position component that makes it better, but bending over makes 
it worse. She denies blurry vision, but reports nausea, 
photophobia, phonophobia and bilateral eye tearing. The headache 
is currently ___ in severity. She takes Topamax for headache 
prophylaxis without effect. She does wake up at night secondary 
to pain. 

She also complains of worsening of her neuropathy pain with 
stabbing pain in knees and feet and elbows to fingertips. This 
also worsened after the lumbar puncture. She can't sleep because 
the sheets bother her and cause her pain. She has been to a lot 
of specialists but reports no one can seem to treat her 
adequately. She says she needed a morphine drip on her last

and craniocervical regions are unremarkable.  There is no evidence of Chiari
malformation seen.

MRV of the head demonstrates normal flow signal in the superior sagittal and
transverse sinuses as well as in the deep venous system.  There is no evidence
of dural venous sinus thrombosis.
